title: Rooms in Rust from the interior kit: 2 m modules with real reveals, trims, windows, props and peeling-paint decals, never untextured boxes
note: Build an indoor level from docs/examples/interior-kit: copy assets/kit, place its 2 m modules and props with frame.model_with, never greybox boxes.
intent: Untextured boxes, box stacks and a dado that is one scan tinted read as a prototype. Copy docs/examples/interior-kit/assets/kit/ to assets/kit/ and lay the level out in 2 m wall modules as that example's game.rs does: wall, wall-window or wall-door (the opening's sides are its reveals), each painted face with its -paint coat and -trims; windows dressed with window-frame, window-sill, window-sash, window-glass or window-glass-broken and a grille; door-frame and door; beam, light-fitting with light-tube, radiator, desk, chair, lockers, teacher-desk, blackboard, debris-pile, fallen-plaster, paper-litter. Each GLB has one material named for its role: draw it with frame.model_with and that role's material, a CC0 scan with .with_world_uv(metres) and .with_stochastic_tiling(true) for plaster, paint and concrete, kit/trim_*.webp for trims and kit/props_*.webp for props. Give radiator, desk, chair, lockers and the sunburst grille their -lod1 level with Model::with_levels. Colliders come from the same plan as the draw. Wear is the kit's decals: peel_edge under the dado rail, leak under sills, grime_base along the floor.
port: The facet that owns the level's layout owns the module plan, its colliders and its probes; a facet that dresses a room places the kit's props and decals and tags them.

evidence.source: src/game-template-rust/docs/examples/interior-kit (the kit, its script and a corridor and classroom built from it)
evidence.note: 42 one-material GLBs on a 2 m grid, a trim sheet, a props atlas and peeling-paint decals from CC0 scans; the example draws, collides and decals them from one plan.
Material::with_world_uv and with_stochastic_tiling keep a scan at its real size on any piece; decals lay wear onto a surface.
A room is built, not boxed: greybox, scans, then the interior kit's modules and dressing.
